title.en: What a plan is, and why the best one sits in a corner
title.zh: 什么是“计划”，为什么最好的计划总在角上

description.en: Shader Electronics has two products and two departments with limited hours. You hold plans in your hand, slide a profit line over them, and see why only corners need checking and which limits matter.
description.zh: Shader Electronics 有两种产品、两个工时有限的车间。你亲手拿着各种“计划”，把利润线推过它们，看清为什么只需要检查角点、哪些限制真正起作用。

name.en: Reading a linear program as a picture
name.zh: 把线性规划当作一幅图来读

description.en: Making as much as possible of the product with the higher profit per unit
description.zh: 把单位利润更高的产品尽量多做

description.en: Believing the best plan is a balanced one in the middle of the allowed set
description.zh: 以为最优计划是可行域中间那种“均衡”的计划

description.en: Believing every limit in the model holds the best plan
description.zh: 以为模型里的每条限制都卡住了最优计划

text.en: Shader Electronics makes two products: the **x-pod**, a portable music player, and the **BlueBerry**, a phone with a colour screen. Each needs time in two departments, and each department has only so many hours this period.
text.zh: Shader Electronics 生产两种产品：**x-pod**（便携式音乐播放器）和 **BlueBerry**（彩屏手机）。每种产品都要占用两个车间的工时，而每个车间这个周期的工时是有限的。

text.en: The manager asks: *how many of each should we make to earn the most?* Making more of one leaves fewer hours for the other, so this is a question about **how to split** limited hours. Every possible answer is a pair of numbers, x-pods and BlueBerrys. Call such a pair a **plan**.
text.zh: 经理问：*每种做多少，才能赚得最多？* 一种做多了，另一种能用的工时就少了，所以这是在问**怎样分配**有限的工时。每个可能的答案都是一对数：x-pod 几个、BlueBerry 几个。这样的一对数叫一个**计划**。

prompt.en: Could Shader make **40 x-pods and 40 BlueBerrys** this period?
prompt.zh: 这个周期里，Shader 能做 **40 个 x-pod 和 40 个 BlueBerry** 吗？

label.en: Yes. It would earn \$480.

feedback.en: \$480 is what it *would* earn, but the hours do not exist: the plan needs 280 electronic hours (240 available) and 120 assembly hours (100 available).
feedback.zh: \$480 是它*会*赚的钱，但工时不够：这个计划要 280 个电子工时（只有 240）和 120 个装配工时（只有 100）。

label.en: No: it runs out of electronic hours only.
label.zh: 不能：只是电子工时不够。

feedback.en: Check assembly too: $2 \cdot 40 + 1 \cdot 40 = 120$, and only 100 are available.

label.en: No: it runs out of both.
label.zh: 不能：两个车间的工时都不够。

explain.en: Electronic: $4 \cdot 40 + 3 \cdot 40 = 280 > 240$. Assembly: $2 \cdot 40 + 1 \cdot 40 = 120 > 100$. A plan has to keep **every** limit at the same time.
explain.zh: 电子：$4 \cdot 40 + 3 \cdot 40 = 280 > 240$。装配：$2 \cdot 40 + 1 \cdot 40 = 120 > 100$。一个计划必须**同时**守住**每一条**限制。

caption.en: Each point is a plan: $x_1$ x-pods and $x_2$ BlueBerrys. The two lines are the departments’ hours; the green set is every plan that keeps both. The numbers: what the plan in hand earns, and how much of each department it uses.
caption.zh: 每个点是一个计划：$x_1$ 个 x-pod、$x_2$ 个 BlueBerry。两条线是两个车间的工时；绿色区域是同时守住两条限制的全部计划。数字是手里这个计划赚多少、各用了每个车间多少工时。

text.en: Inside the green set both departments have hours to spare. **On** a line, that department is used up completely. **Past** a line, the plan asks for hours that do not exist.
text.zh: 绿色区域里，两个车间都有富余。**落在**线上，那个车间的工时正好用完。**越过**线，这个计划要的工时就不存在了。

prompt.en: The plan with 20 x-pods and 40 BlueBerrys: how much profit does it earn?
prompt.zh: 20 个 x-pod 加 40 个 BlueBerry 的计划，利润是多少？

prompt.en: Of all the allowed plans, which kind earns the most? Decide before you look.
prompt.zh: 在所有允许的计划里，哪一类赚得最多？先想好，再往下看。

label.en: As many x-pods as possible (50 x-pods, no BlueBerrys), because an x-pod earns more per unit.
label.zh: x-pod 尽量多做（50 个，不做 BlueBerry），因为 x-pod 每件赚得多。

feedback.en: That plan earns \$350 and leaves 40 electronic hours idle. Swap one x-pod for two BlueBerrys: assembly hours balance ($-2 + 2$), the idle electronic hours cover the extra 2, and profit rises by $10 - 7 = 3$. Keep swapping until electronic hours run out too.
feedback.zh: 这个计划赚 \$350，还有 40 个电子工时闲着。拿一个 x-pod 换两个 BlueBerry：装配工时刚好抵消（$-2 + 2$），闲着的电子工时够用，利润涨 $10 - 7 = 3$。一直换到电子工时也用完为止。

label.en: Only BlueBerrys, as many as the electronic hours allow (80).
label.zh: 只做 BlueBerry，做到电子工时用完（80 个）。

feedback.en: That plan earns \$400 and leaves 20 assembly hours idle. Replace 4 BlueBerrys by 3 x-pods: the same 12 electronic hours, 2 more assembly hours, and profit rises by $21 - 20 = 1$.
feedback.zh: 这个计划赚 \$400，还有 20 个装配工时闲着。把 4 个 BlueBerry 换成 3 个 x-pod：电子工时同样是 12，装配多用 2 个，利润涨 $21 - 20 = 1$。

label.en: A balanced plan in the middle of the green set, with hours left in both departments.
label.zh: 绿色区域中间的一个“均衡”计划，两个车间都还有富余。

feedback.en: Hours left over earn nothing: from any plan with spare hours in both departments you can make a little more of something and earn more. The best plan cannot be inside.
feedback.zh: 剩下的工时不赚钱：只要两个车间都有富余，就总能多做一点什么、多赚一点。最好的计划不可能在里面。

label.en: A plan that uses up the hours of both departments.
label.zh: 把两个车间的工时都用完的计划。

explain.en: The next page shows why: the best plan is where a profit line leaves the green set last.
explain.zh: 下一页会让你看到原因：最好的计划是利润线最后离开绿色区域的地方。

text.en: A profit of \$300 can be reached by many plans: every point on the line $7x_1 + 5x_2 = 300$ earns exactly that. A profit of \$350 is another line, parallel to the first and further out.
text.zh: 很多计划都能赚到 \$300：直线 $7x_1 + 5x_2 = 300$ 上的每个点正好赚这么多。\$350 是另一条线，和第一条平行、更靠外。

caption.en: The profit line for the level in hand. Thick: the plans on it that are allowed.
caption.zh: 手里这个利润水平对应的利润线。粗的部分：线上被允许的计划。

text.en: As the line slides out, its thick part shrinks. The last allowed plan it touches is the **best plan**. The green set has straight sides, so the line always leaves it at a **corner**, or along a whole edge if the line is parallel to that edge.
text.zh: 线往外推，粗的部分越来越短。它最后碰到的那个被允许的计划就是**最优计划**。绿色区域的边是直的，所以线总是在**角**上离开；线和某条边平行时，就沿着整条边离开。

prompt.en: Why does the last plan the profit line touches have to be a corner (or a whole edge)?
prompt.zh: 为什么利润线最后碰到的那个计划一定是个角（或一整条边）？

label.en: Profit lines are parallel and move out together, and a straight line sliding over a polygon leaves it last at a corner.
label.zh: 利润线互相平行、一起往外推，而一条直线扫过多边形，最后离开的地方是个角。

label.en: Because corners are where the most hours are used.
label.zh: 因为角上用的工时最多。

feedback.en: Using the most hours is not the reason. A profit line can leave along a whole edge, and the edge’s ends are corners too.
feedback.zh: 用工时最多不是原因。利润线也可能沿整条边离开，而边的两端同样是角。

label.en: Because the profit line is curved and touches the set at a point.
label.zh: 因为利润线是弯的，只在一点碰到区域。

feedback.en: Every limit and the profit are linear: straight lines only.
feedback.zh: 每条限制和利润都是线性的：只有直线。

explain.en: This is why a solver only has to look at corners, however many variables there are.
explain.zh: 这就是为什么不管有多少变量，求解器只需要看角点。

caption.en: The four corners of the allowed set and what each earns.
caption.zh: 允许区域的四个角，以及每个角赚多少。

text.en: So there is no need to try every plan: find the corners, work out the profit at each, take the largest. A corner is where two lines meet, so you find it by solving their two equations together.
text.zh: 所以没必要试遍所有计划：找出各个角，算出每个角的利润，取最大的。角是两条线相交的地方，解这两条线的方程组就能找到它。

prompt.en: The electronic line $4x_1 + 3x_2 = 240$ and the assembly line $2x_1 + x_2 = 100$ meet at one point. What is $x_1$ there?
prompt.zh: 电子线 $4x_1 + 3x_2 = 240$ 和装配线 $2x_1 + x_2 = 100$ 交于一点。那里的 $x_1$ 是多少？

explain.en: Multiply the second equation by 3: $6x_1 + 3x_2 = 300$. Subtract the first: $2x_1 = 60$, so $x_1 = 30$ and $x_2 = 100 - 60 = 40$.

text.en: At the best plan both departments’ hours are used up. Now move the walls and watch the best plan and its profit.
text.zh: 在最优计划处两个车间的工时都用完了。现在移动这两面墙，看最优计划和它的利润怎么变。

caption.en: Each wall can be moved. Thick walls are the limits that hold the best plan.
caption.zh: 每面墙都可以移动。粗的墙是卡住最优计划的那些限制。

text.en: A limit the best plan uses up completely is **binding**. A limit with hours left over is **slack**. Moving a binding wall changes the best profit; moving a slack wall changes nothing.
text.zh: 最优计划把某条限制用完，这条限制就是**紧的**（binding）；还有富余的是**松的**（slack）。移动紧的墙，最优利润会变；移动松的墙，什么都不变。

prompt.en: Electronic hours go up from 240 to 250. By how much does the best profit rise?
prompt.zh: 电子工时从 240 增加到 250。最优利润增加多少？

explain.en: The new corner solves $4x_1 + 3x_2 = 250$ and $2x_1 + x_2 = 100$: $x_1 = 25$, $x_2 = 50$, profit $7 \cdot 25 + 5 \cdot 50 = 425$, which is \$15 more than \$410: \$1.50 per extra hour. The report calls it the **shadow price** (lesson 3).

title.zh: 一条永远不起作用的限制

caption.en: A third limit: packing capacity, 120 units.
caption.zh: 第三条限制：包装能力 120 件。

text.en: The best plan packs only $30 + 40 = 70$ units, so packing is **slack**: there is room to spare, and moving its wall changes nothing. Such a limit is called redundant when it can never bind.
text.zh: 最优计划只包 $30 + 40 = 70$ 件，所以包装是**松的**：有富余，移动它的墙什么都不变。一条永远不会起作用的限制叫作冗余的。

prompt.en: Packing capacity rises from 120 to 150 units. What happens to the best profit?
prompt.zh: 包装能力从 120 件提高到 150 件。最优利润会怎样？

label.en: It rises.
label.zh: 上升。

feedback.en: Only a binding limit can raise profit when relaxed. The best plan packs 70 of the 120 units, so 50 are idle.
feedback.zh: 只有紧的限制放松才会提高利润。最优计划只包 120 件里的 70 件，有 50 件闲着。

label.en: It stays at \$410.
label.zh: 保持 \$410 不变。

label.en: It falls.
label.zh: 下降。

feedback.en: Relaxing a limit never makes the best plan worse: every old plan is still allowed.
feedback.zh: 放松限制不会让最优计划变差：原来允许的计划仍然都允许。

explain.en: The best plan uses 70 of 120 packing units: slack. A slack limit can be moved without changing the best plan.
explain.zh: 最优计划只用了 120 件包装能力里的 70 件：松的。松的限制随便移动，最优计划都不变。

title.en: Three ways a picture surprises you

text.en: The picture does not always have one best corner. Here are the three surprises the exam can ask about.
text.zh: 图并不总是有唯一的最优角。下面是考试可能问到的三种意外。

caption.en: Profit $4x_1 + 3x_2$ is parallel to the electronic wall.
caption.zh: 利润 $4x_1 + 3x_2$ 和电子线平行。

text.en: **Alternative optima.** The profit line leaves along a whole edge, so many plans tie at \$240. A solver reports one corner of that edge; any plan between its two ends is just as good.
text.zh: **多个最优解。** 利润线沿着整条边离开，所以很多计划并列在 \$240。求解器只报告这条边的一个端点；两端之间的任何计划一样好。

caption.en: A contract demands at least 60 x-pods, but assembly allows only 50.
caption.zh: 合同要求至少 60 个 x-pod，但装配最多只允许 50 个。

text.en: **Infeasible.** No plan keeps every limit, so there is no best plan. The fix is in the model or in the promises, not in the solver.
text.zh: **无可行解。** 没有任何计划能同时守住所有限制，所以没有最优计划。要改的是模型或承诺，不是求解器。

caption.en: Only minimums: the allowed set runs off the page.
caption.zh: 只有下限：允许区域一直延伸出画面。

text.en: **Unbounded.** Profit can grow forever. In a real business this means a limit is missing from the model, never that profit is infinite.
text.zh: **无界。** 利润可以无限增大。在真实的业务里，这说明模型漏了某条限制，而不是利润真的无限。

prompt.en: A solver reports **infeasible**. What does the picture look like?
prompt.zh: 求解器报告**无可行解**。图是什么样的？

label.en: The allowed set is empty: the limits contradict each other.
label.zh: 允许区域是空的：限制互相矛盾。

label.en: The allowed set runs off the page.
label.zh: 允许区域一直延伸出画面。

feedback.en: That is **unbounded**: profit has no top.
feedback.zh: 那是**无界**：利润没有上限。

label.en: The profit line is parallel to a wall.
label.zh: 利润线和某面墙平行。

feedback.en: That gives many best plans (alternative optima), not none.
feedback.zh: 那是有很多最优计划（多个最优解），不是没有。

explain.en: Infeasible: no plan keeps every limit, the allowed set is empty.
explain.zh: 无可行解：没有任何计划能守住所有限制，允许区域是空的。

text.en: Everything you did has a name, and the exam uses the names. The picture and the model are one thing seen twice.
text.zh: 你做过的每件事都有名字，考试要用这些名字。图和模型是同一件事的两种样子。

rows.en: **Objective function**: what you maximise or minimise
rows.zh: **目标函数**：要最大化或最小化的量

rows.en: the profit line’s slope, and which way is “more”
rows.zh: 利润线的斜率，和哪边是“更多”

rows.en: the allowed set, and its best corner
rows.zh: 允许区域，和它最好的角

text.en: Three assumptions keep the picture straight. It is **deterministic**: every number (the profits, the hours per unit, the hours available) is known for certain. It is **proportional**: twice the units need twice the hours and earn twice the profit. It is **divisible**: a fraction of a unit is allowed. “Programming” here means *modelling*, not coding. LP helps managers share out resources, the four M and a T: machinery, labour, money, materials and time.
text.zh: 三条假设让这幅图保持“直”。**确定性**：每个数（利润、单位工时、可用工时）都是已知的。**成比例**：单位数翻倍，工时和利润也翻倍。**可分**：可以做不足一个的零头。这里的 “programming” 是*建模*，不是写代码。LP 帮经理分配资源：设备、人力、资金、材料和时间。

rows.zh: 描述统计、概率、分布（第 7、8 周）
一元和多元回归（第 9、10 周）

rows.en: linear and integer programming, decision analysis (weeks 1 to 6)
rows.zh: 线性和整数规划、决策分析（第 1 到 6 周）

title.en: Recall: where the best plan sits

prompt.en: A profit line slides out over an allowed set. Where does it leave it?
prompt.zh: 一条利润线从里往外扫过一个允许区域。它在哪里离开？

label.en: At a corner, or along a whole edge if parallel to it.
label.zh: 在一个角上；和某条边平行时，沿整条边。

label.en: In the middle, where the limits are balanced.
label.zh: 在中间，限制取得平衡的地方。

feedback.en: Spare hours earn nothing; the line is still moving out there.
feedback.zh: 富余的工时不赚钱；线在那里还能继续往外。

label.en: At the plan with the most of the dearer product.
label.zh: 在尽量多做利润更高那个产品的计划上。

feedback.en: The swaps on the prediction page beat it.
feedback.zh: 预测页里的“换”能打败它。

explain.en: Corner, or an edge: the first place a straight line can no longer stay inside a polygon.
explain.zh: 角，或一条边：直线刚好无法再待在多边形里的地方。

prompt.en: At the best plan, a department uses 70 of its 120 hours. Moving that limit to 130 hours changes the best profit by:
prompt.zh: 在最优计划处，某个车间用了 120 个工时里的 70 个。把这条限制移到 130 个工时，最优利润变化：

label.en: Nothing: the limit is slack.
label.zh: 没有变化：这条限制是松的。

label.en: Ten hours times the profit per hour.
label.zh: 10 个工时乘以每工时利润。

feedback.en: That is for a binding limit. This one has 50 hours idle.
feedback.zh: 那是紧的限制才会有的。这条还闲着 50 个工时。

label.en: It falls by ten hours’ worth.
label.zh: 减少 10 个工时的价值。

explain.en: 70 of 120 used: slack. Only a binding limit changes the best profit when moved.
explain.zh: 120 里用了 70：松。只有紧的限制移动时才改变最优利润。
